Name: compression_based_text_quality_assessment
Title: Using Compression Efficiency as a Unified Metric for Text Quality Assessment
Experiment: Develop a framework that uses compression ratios from multiple language models to automatically detect and classify problematic text characteristics (ambiguity, malformation, controversy). Train classifiers on datasets where text quality issues correlate with compression inefficiency, then validate on diverse test sets including social media, legal documents, and scientific papers.

Name: logarithmic_compression_numerical_representations
Title: Logarithmic Scaling in Neural Number Representations: Implications for Compression Efficiency
Experiment: Systematically probe LLaMA models across different scales with numerical sequences spanning orders of magnitude, extracting internal representations at each layer. Compare compression ratios when encoding numbers using the model's native representation versus uniform linear encoding, testing whether the logarithmic-like scaling mirrors optimal information-theoretic compression for natural number distributions.

Name: compression_aware_probing_boundaries
Title: Compression-Optimal Feature Extraction: Beyond Orthogonal Decision Boundaries in Neural Language Models
Experiment: Compare traditional orthogonal probing methods against mass-mean probing across multiple compression tasks (text prediction, lossless compression, and semantic compression) using transformer language models. Measure both decision boundary quality and feature direction alignment with optimal compression codes, testing whether non-orthogonal boundaries discovered by mass-mean probing lead to better compression ratios and more efficient representations.

Name: compression_based_qa_evaluation
Title: Evaluating Question Answering Through Compression-Based Truth Metrics
Experiment: Design compression-based metrics that correlate answer quality with how well correct answers compress given the question context, compared to incorrect answers. Test on multiple QA datasets by measuring compression ratios of answer candidates and comparing against human judgments and traditional QA evaluation metrics.

Name: causal_truth_compression_intervention
Title: Causal Intervention Analysis of Truth vs Correlation in Compressed Language Representations
Experiment: Design controlled datasets where truth and correlated features (syntax, frequency, sentiment) are systematically decoupled, then train compression-based language models on these datasets. Apply causal intervention techniques to selectively ablate correlated features while preserving truth content, measuring whether probes maintain accuracy when correlational shortcuts are removed.

Name: compression_based_belief_detection
Title: Detecting AI Deception Through Differential Compression Analysis of Internal Representations
Experiment: Train language models to compress sequences containing both truthful and deceptive agent statements, measuring compression ratios across different context windows. Compare compression efficiency when models process authentic vs. fabricated internal monologues, hypothesizing that deceptive content requires more bits due to inconsistencies with the model's learned patterns of genuine reasoning.

Name: compression_based_instruction_taxonomy
Title: Compression-Theoretic Framework for Distinguishing Language Model Capabilities
Experiment: Develop compression-based metrics to quantitatively distinguish between question-answering, instruction-following, and pure language modeling by measuring the Kolmogorov complexity of model outputs under different prompting paradigms. Train models on identical datasets but evaluate their compression efficiency when performing factual QA versus creative instruction-following versus next-token prediction, establishing whether these capabilities exhibit distinct information-theoretic signatures.

Name: compression_based_truthfulness_detection
Title: Truthfulness Detection in LLMs Through Compression-Based Linear Probing
Experiment: Train linear probes on LLM internal representations to detect truthfulness while simultaneously measuring the compressibility of true vs false statements using arithmetic coding. Compare probe accuracy with compression ratios across different layers to identify whether truthful statements exhibit better compression properties and whether this correlates with the strength of linear truthfulness directions.
